purpose: 2020 calibration case for operational consumer-bill indices. Published allowances remain the historical bill baseline; same-year indices are diagnostics, not independent validation or automatic bill substitutions.

bsuos.source: Published 2020 NESO Historic SF BSUoS dataset, aggregated over 1 January-31 December (GBP 1,992,748,248.40 / 439,206,084.74 MWh); and the published 2020 Ofgem BSUoS allowance. The bridge indexes the allowance to gross PyPSA redispatch MWh per MWh demand, not PyPSA bid/offer cost. Pre-April 2023 BSUoS allocation differs from current final-demand-only recovery, so this outturn is a comparator, not a household allocation.

losses.source: Use the resistance-weighted flow-squared (I2R) proxy from the complete physical balancing runs as a same-year calibrated index for the published 2020 GB-average allowance. The LP's represented AC losses remain zero, so the proxy is not a physical power-flow result. It excludes distribution and regional supplier loss factors; future use needs a second historical calibration or a validated lossy network formulation.

imbalance.source: Published 2020 Ofgem imbalance allowance in the component register; gross PyPSA redispatch MWh per MWh demand is the same-year calibration index.

capacity_market.source: 2020 published Capacity Market allowance indexed only to modelled wind-and-solar residual peak. This is a scenario assumption, not a Capacity Market auction-payment calculation.

tnuos.source: 2020 published TNUoS allowance indexed only to represented transmission capacity. Replace with NESO allowed-revenue and charging allocation for future bill use.

duos_unit.source: 2020 published DUoS volumetric allowance held at baseline. The transmission model does not represent DNO assets or charging allocation.

duos_fixed.source: 2020 published DUoS fixed allowance held at baseline. The transmission model does not represent domestic accounts, meters or DNO charging allocation.

fit.source: FiT remains unrepresented in the current support labels. Add FiT-labelled generation and Ofgem tariff/levelisation inputs before using this bridge.
